title: Local nonlinear constraint construction with explicit analytic obligations

items.title: Bounded-domain charged conformal problem
items.design_state: Defines the bounded smooth domain, Hölder spaces, zero-boundary trace, fixed source profile, dimensionless charge parameter, and exact time-symmetric flat-seed scalar equation.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty, bounded, connected open set with smooth boundary, meaning each boundary point has Euclidean coordinates in which $\Omega$ is one side of a smooth graph. Use Euclidean coordinates $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$, and set $\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2$. Fix $0<\alpha<1$, a real function $S\in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $S\geq0$, and a real dimensionless parameter $\varepsilon$. For $g:\overline\Omega\to\mathbb R$, define $[g]_{0,\alpha}:=\sup_{x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/|x-y|^\alpha$ and $\|g\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}:=\sup_{\overline\Omega}|g|+[g]_{0,\alpha}$. Define $C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ to consist of functions whose derivatives through order $2$ on $\Omega$ extend continuously to $\overline\Omega$ and whose norm

$$\|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}:=\sum_{|\beta|\leq2}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta u|+\sum_{|\beta|=2}[D^\beta u]_{0,\alpha}$$

is finite, where $\beta$ is a multi-index. Write $X:=\{u\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):u|_{\partial\Omega}=0\}$, with its inherited norm, and $Y:=C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$. The bounded-domain charged conformal problem is to find $u\in X$ such that $\psi:=1+u>0$ on $\overline\Omega$ and

$$-8\Delta\psi=2\varepsilon^2 S\psi^{-3}\quad\hbox{in }\Omega,\qquad \psi|_{\partial\Omega}=1.$$

In the time-symmetric flat-seed specialization $h=\psi^4\delta$, $K=0$, and $\Lambda=0$, the scalar equation is the Hamiltonian constraint from the conformal electrovacuum transformation when $S=|\bar E_0|_\delta^2+|\bar B_0|_\delta^2$ for independently prescribed divergence-free base fields and the actual seed fields are $\bar E=\varepsilon\bar E_0$, $\bar B=\varepsilon\bar B_0$. In geometric length coordinates, $\psi,\varepsilon$ are dimensionless, $\bar E_0,\bar B_0$ have units of inverse length, and $S$ has units of inverse length squared. The definition does not assert existence, uniqueness, a momentum constraint, or an asymptotically Euclidean or puncture solution.

references.title: A. I. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009)
references.locator: Section III.A, equations (3.1)-(3.12); the local definition specializes the Hamiltonian constraint to a flat time-symmetric seed.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012), author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1
references.locator: Sections 6.2.3 and 6.4.2, equations (6.14)-(6.22) and (6.81); conformal metric and constraint conventions.

items.title: Local Banach implicit-function supplier
items.design_state: Local contraction proof of the one-parameter Banach implicit-function result used by the nonlinear branch.
items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, let $U\subset X\times\mathbb R$ be open in the max product norm, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable. Assume $F(0,0)=0$ and that $L:=D_xF(0,0):X\to Y$ is a bounded linear isomorphism. Then there are $\rho,\epsilon_0>0$ and a unique $C^1$ map $x:(-\epsilon_0,\epsilon_0)\to B_X(0,\rho)$ such that $x(0)=0$ and $F(x(\epsilon),\epsilon)=0$; every zero in $B_X(0,\rho)\times(-\epsilon_0,\epsilon_0)$ lies on this graph. Its derivative is

$$x'(\epsilon)=-D_xF(x(\epsilon),\epsilon)^{-1}D_\epsilon F(x(\epsilon),\epsilon).$$

references.title: Chin-Lung Wang, Banach Calculus, National Taiwan University lecture notes (2012; complete 16-page PDF)
references.locator: §3.1 and §3.3, PDF pp. 9-11; contraction mapping and the Banach implicit-function theorem.

references.title: John B. Conway, Functional Analysis, Chapter XII (University of Colorado lecture chapter)
references.locator: Chapter XII, Theorem 12.8 and its contraction-mapping proof, printed pp. 256-257.

items.title: Local energy and zero-boundary closure for the charged constraint problem
items.design_state: Owned local analytic supplier completing the approved Dirichlet inverse proof route; no independent acceptance asserted.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded smooth domain and choose $R>0$ with $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^3$. Write $H^1_0(\Omega)$ for the $H^1$ closure of the compactly supported smooth functions. Then $\|v\|_{L^2}\le2R\|\nabla v\|_{L^2}$ for every $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. A function $u\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ represents an element of $H^1_0(\Omega)$ if and only if $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014), Chapter 4, zero-boundary Poincare and trace arguments

items.title: Newtonian cancellation and the three-dimensional Holder bound
items.design_state: Owned local analytic supplier completing the approved Dirichlet inverse proof route; no independent acceptance asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $0<\alpha<1$, $R>0$, and let $g:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be globally $\alpha$-Hölder with support in $B_{2R}(0)$. Put $Ng(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(y)/(4\pi|x-y|)\,dy$. Then $Ng\in C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, $-\Delta Ng=g$, and

$$\sum_{j=0}^2R^j\|D^jNg\|_{\infty;B_R}+R^{2+\alpha}[D^2Ng]_{\alpha;B_R}\le C_\alpha R^2\bigl(\|g\|_\infty+R^\alpha[g]_\alpha\bigr).$$

The estimate uses the displayed scaled norms and is uniform in $R$ and $g$.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (2014), Section 2.7, Newtonian cancellation and Holder estimates

items.title: Flat Dirichlet Holder estimate by normal-jet lifting and reflection
items.design_state: Owned local analytic supplier completing the approved Dirichlet inverse proof route; no independent acceptance asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and fix $0<\alpha<1$. Put $B_R^+=B_R(0)\cap\{x_3>0\}$ and $T_R=B_R(0)\cap\{x_3=0\}$. Suppose $u$ is bounded and $C^2$ up to the flat face locally in $B_R\cap\{x_3\ge0\}$, $\Delta u=f$ in $B_R^+$, $u=0$ on $T_R$, and $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(\overline{B_R^+})$. There is no condition on the curved boundary and no requirement that $f|_{T_R}=0$. Then

$$\sum_{j=0}^2R^j\|D^ju\|_{\infty;B_{R/2}^+}+R^{2+\alpha}[D^2u]_{\alpha;B_{R/2}^+}\le C_\alpha\bigl(\|u\|_{\infty;B_R^+}+R^2\|f\|_\infty+R^{2+\alpha}[f]_\alpha\bigr).$$

The derivatives extend Hölder continuously to the flat face. The constant is independent of $R$ and of any higher derivative of a smooth approximant.

references.title: Xu-Jia Wang, Schauder Estimates for Elliptic and Parabolic Equations (2006), Theorem 1 and Theorem 1-prime, pages 1-3

items.title: Global Dirichlet Holder estimate from finite flattened charts
items.design_state: Owned local analytic supplier completing the approved Dirichlet inverse proof route; no independent acceptance asserted.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every bounded smooth domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ and $0<\alpha<1$ there is $C=C(\Omega,\alpha)$ such that every $u\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with zero boundary restriction satisfies

$$\|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\bigl(\|\Delta u\|_{C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}+\|u\|_{C^0(\overline\Omega)}\bigr).$$

The Hölder norms are the full derivative-supremum plus top-seminorm norms. The constant does not depend on higher derivatives of $u$; this is an a priori estimate, in particular for smooth approximants, not an assumed weak-to-classical existence theorem.

references.title: Xu-Jia Wang, Schauder Estimates for Elliptic and Parabolic Equations (2006), pages 1-3, local estimates and freezing
Armin Schikorra, Partial Differential Equations I & II, Sections 8.8-8.9, finite boundary-chart global estimates

items.title: Dirichlet Hölder inverse required by the constraint branch
items.design_state: Constructs the weak zero-boundary solution by Poincare and Lax-Milgram, then applies the exact published weak-to-strong Dirichlet Schauder supplier; the design-required local Schauder reconstruction is escalated in batch notes.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For the domain $\Omega$ and exponent $\alpha$ of *Bounded-domain charged conformal problem*, let $X=\{u\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):u|_{\partial\Omega}=0\}$ and $Y=C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with the full norms specified there; the zero subscript denotes zero boundary restriction, not compact support. Then

$$-\Delta:X\longrightarrow Y$$

is a bounded linear isomorphism. Consequently $A:=-8\Delta:X\to Y$ is a bounded linear isomorphism and its inverse obeys $\|A^{-1}f\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}\leq C(\Omega,\alpha)\|f\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}$.

references.title: David Gilbarg and Neil S. Trudinger, Elliptic Partial Differential Equations of Second Order (2001)
references.locator: Chapter 4, Theorems 4.6 and 4.8 on Poisson Hölder estimates; Chapter 6, Lemma 6.18 and Theorem 6.19, printed pp. 111-112.

references.title: Armin Schikorra, Partial Differential Equations I & II (version October 1, 2025; complete 281-page graduate lecture notes)
references.locator: §8.8, Theorem 8.28, and §8.9, Theorem 8.30, printed pp. 151-153; §8.8 states the boundary estimate and refers to Gilbarg-Trudinger for the flattening proof.

references.title: Xu-Jia Wang, Schauder Estimates for Elliptic and Parabolic Equations (Australian National University, 2006; complete 7-page note)
references.locator: §1, Theorems 1 and 10, printed pp. 1-2; Theorem 10 gives the half-ball zero-boundary estimate by odd reflection for an already classical solution.

items.title: Positive Hölder cubic map is continuously differentiable
items.design_state: Local Hölder-algebra estimate proving C1 regularity of the positive cubic source map needed by the branch theorem.
items.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y=C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ be the Hölder spaces with the norms specified in *Bounded-domain charged conformal problem*, and let $S\in Y$ be its source. The inclusion $X\hookrightarrow Y$ is bounded. The set $\mathcal U:=\{u\in Y:\min_{\overline\Omega}(1+u)>0\}$ is open, and

$$N_S:\mathcal U\to Y,\qquad N_S(u):=S(1+u)^{-3},$$

is continuously Fréchet differentiable with $DN_S(u)[h]=-3S(1+u)^{-4}h$ for every $u\in\mathcal U$ and $h\in Y$.

references.title: Chin-Lung Wang, Banach Calculus, National Taiwan University lecture notes (2012; complete 16-page PDF)
references.locator: §2.1-2.4, PDF pp. 4-8; Fréchet derivatives, parameter derivatives, and the Banach chain rule.

references.title: John B. Conway, Functional Analysis, Chapter XII (University of Colorado lecture chapter)
references.locator: Chapter XII, the Banach calculus and operator-norm framework preceding Theorem 12.8, printed pp. 248-254.

items.title: Small charged Dirichlet conformal branch
items.design_state: Establishes the unique local small-amplitude Dirichlet branch, positivity, and the second-order expansion with a C2,alpha O(epsilon^4) remainder.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For the problem of *Bounded-domain charged conformal problem*, there are $\rho>0$, $\varepsilon_0>0$, and $C<\infty$ such that for each $|\varepsilon|<\varepsilon_0$ there is exactly one solution $u_\varepsilon\in X$ with $\|u_\varepsilon\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}<\rho$. The corresponding $\psi_\varepsilon=1+u_\varepsilon$ satisfies $\psi_\varepsilon\geq1$ on $\overline\Omega$. If $v\in X$ is the unique solution of $-8\Delta v=2S$ in $\Omega$, $v=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, then

$$\|u_\varepsilon-\varepsilon^2v\|_{C^{2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\leq C|\varepsilon|^4.$$

The constants may depend on $\Omega,\alpha,S$, and the uniqueness is only in the fixed neighborhood $\|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}<\rho$; no global uniqueness, asymptotically Euclidean solution, puncture solution, or non-CMC result is asserted. The $O(\varepsilon^4)$ statement means the displayed bound for all $|\varepsilon|<\varepsilon_0$.

references.title: David Gilbarg and Neil S. Trudinger, Elliptic Partial Differential Equations of Second Order (2001)
references.locator: Chapter 6, Lemma 6.18 and Theorem 6.19, printed pp. 111-112; boundary Hölder regularity for classical Dirichlet solutions.

references.title: Armin Schikorra, Partial Differential Equations I & II (version October 1, 2025; complete 281-page graduate lecture notes)
references.locator: §8.9, Theorem 8.30, printed pp. 151-153; weak-to-strong regularity from a global Schauder estimate.

references.title: Chin-Lung Wang, Banach Calculus, National Taiwan University lecture notes (2012; complete 16-page PDF)
references.locator: §3.1 and §3.3, PDF pp. 9-11; contraction and implicit-function methods in Banach spaces.

references.title: John B. Conway, Functional Analysis, Chapter XII (University of Colorado lecture chapter)
references.locator: Chapter XII, Theorem 12.8, printed pp. 256-257; implicit-function theorem proved from contraction mapping.

title: Local nonlinear constraint construction with explicit analytic obligations — Examples

items.title: Constant-field branch on a ball
items.design_state: Checks the local theorem on a ball with constant divergence-free base field and computes the leading Dirichlet coefficient exactly.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=B_R(0)\subset\mathbb R^3$ for a fixed length $R>0$, let $\bar E_0=a\,e_1$ be a constant Euclidean base vector with $a\geq0$ of units inverse length, and let $\bar B_0=0$. The actual fields are $\bar E_\varepsilon=\varepsilon\bar E_0$, $\bar B_\varepsilon=\varepsilon\bar B_0$, so $S=|\bar E_0|^2+|\bar B_0|^2=a^2$ is nonnegative and Hölder continuous, both actual seed fields are divergence-free, and $\varepsilon$ is dimensionless. Under the hypotheses of *Small charged Dirichlet conformal branch*, the bounded-domain equation has a unique local branch with

$$\psi_\varepsilon(x)=1+\varepsilon^2\frac{a^2}{24}\bigl(R^2-|x|^2\bigr)+O_{C^{2,\alpha}}(\varepsilon^4),\qquad \psi_\varepsilon\geq1.$$

This example concerns only the fixed ball and its Dirichlet data.

references.title: A. I. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009)
references.locator: Section III.A, equations (3.1)-(3.12); geometric-normalized seed fields and the time-symmetric scalar constraint.

references.title: David Gilbarg and Neil S. Trudinger, Elliptic Partial Differential Equations of Second Order (2001)
references.locator: Chapter 4, Theorems 4.6 and 4.8; the local example's linear Dirichlet coefficient is computed directly.
